A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedCEO research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EMNIST and CIFAR-10 classification results, runtime comparisons, heterogeneous-client experiments, and DLG privacy attacks.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds interval-sensitivity measurements, AlexNet/CIFAR-10 and LSTM/Sent140 evaluations, and attack-reconstruction PSNR values.

M1.justification: New Section 3.3 proposes an optional scaling adaptation that applies T-tSVD only to the last few model layers. The core FedCEO algorithm, objective, and adaptive threshold remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that the reported experiments use this adaptation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates image classification on EMNIST and CIFAR-10. v2 adds evaluation on the Sent140 text dataset in Appendix C.2.3/Table 6, substantially extending coverage beyond images. Existing image and heterogeneous-client scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The utility comparators remain private FedAvg, PPSGD, and CENTAUR, and the privacy comparisons retain FedAvg and private FedAvg. LDP-FedAvg is renamed UDP-FedAvg without changing Algorithm 1. Table 6 extends the existing comparator set to additional configurations.

E3.justification: v2 adds AlexNet/CIFAR-10 and LSTM/Sent140 configurations, a five-value interval sweep, and PSNR as a reconstruction metric. Existing training budgets and principal privacy settings remain unchanged. The newly specified post-optimization attack placement does not establish that an earlier procedure was changed or rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 3 tests sensitivity to the processing interval I using values 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 under three noise settings. Existing adaptive-threshold comparisons, spectral analysis, heterogeneous-client tests, and DLG attack examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands reported results through Tables 3 and 6. At sigma_g=1.0, the new FedCEO accuracies are 60.73% for AlexNet/CIFAR-10 and 65.70% for LSTM/Sent140. Figure 3 adds PSNR values of 19.73, 10.33, and 10.15 dB for FedAvg, UDP-FedAvg, and FedCEO. Original main-table, runtime, and heterogeneous-client scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1, Equation (8), corrects the nuclear-norm expansion to sum norms of individual Fourier slices. Section 3.3 adds a layerwise computational-complexity expression, and Definition 2.1 explicitly specifies add/remove adjacency. The principal theorem statements and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim flexible cross-client semantic collaboration through tensor optimization, equivalence to truncated tSVD, an order-sqrt(d) improvement in the utility–privacy bound, and superior empirical trade-offs. The additional experiments support these retained contributions without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly explains scalability through narrower, semantically informative final layers. Appendix C.1 adds a claim of hyperparameter robustness, and Section 5.3 explicitly interprets the post-optimization attack as checking that tensor processing preserves DP protection.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly discloses grid-search ranges for lambda, theta, and I while retaining the selected settings. Section 5.3 specifies the attack's placement after tensor optimization. The printed code repository address also changes; the PDFs do not establish its accessibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning private and heterogeneous federated learning, gradient leakage, and the text benchmark, including Wei, Hu, Tsoy, Caldas, Huang, and Fu and colleagues. It also attributes the UDP-FedAvg privacy lemma to Cheng et al. The central positioning against PPSGD, CENTAUR, and independent client-wise spectral processing remains.

P1.justification: Changes include localized language corrections, LDP-to-UDP terminology, updated authors and publication information, and short new scalability and experimental subsections. Most prose, section order, and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 6, renumbers the retained runtime and heterogeneity tables, and annotates Figure 3 with PSNR. Figure 2 moves between columns and receives a shorter caption; retained attack Figures 6–8 are consolidated onto the final page. Most displays preserve their original content and design.

improvement.justification: The added text and AlexNet evaluations broaden empirical support, interval sensitivity helps assess tuning, and PSNR quantifies previously visual attack evidence. Search-range disclosure and the Equation (8) correction improve reproducibility and precision. These provide a clear but limited overall gain: principal findings remain unchanged, while details for the new architectures and experimental uncertainty remain sparse.
